title: Effectiveness of a porcine-derived acellular dermal matrix for peri-implant soft-tissue augmentation: A prospective study
authors: Doan V, Tran HL, Nguyen HN, Vo HBT, Viet H, Vuong The Vinh T. Medicine (Baltimore). 2025 Dec 5;104(49):e46127. doi: 10.1097/MD.0000000000046127.
supports: Clinical study from the botiss mucoderm (porcine collagen soft-tissue matrix) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Abstract, verbatim (no separate conclusion section): “Adequate peri-implant soft tissue is essential for functional and aesthetic success. Autologous grafts are effective but limited by morbidity. This study assessed a porcine-derived acellular dermal matrix (PADM) for anterior maxillary soft-tissue augmentation. 31 patients with implants in the anterior maxilla underwent PADM grafting. Keratinized gingival thickness, width (KGW), zenith-incisal edge distance, and shrinkage rate were measured at baseline (T0), immediate postoperative (T1), 1 month (T2), and 3 months (T3). Aesthetic outcomes were assessed with the pink aesthetic score, and pain with a numeric rating scale. Data were analyzed using Friedman and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Keratinized gingival thickness increased from 0.69 ± 0.30 mm at T0 to 2.40 ± 0.63 mm at T1 (P < .001), decreasing to 1.55 ± 0.41 mm at T3 but remaining above baseline. KGW remained stable.
